diagnostic_evidence.quote: we use the preceding inequality on each of the finitely many connected components and sum over the latter.

issues.failure_explanation: For disconnected $\Omega$ the kernel of $\BD$ consists of rigid deformations chosen independently on each component, not of global affine maps, and Assumption assump:dom (norm property on the global affine maps $Ax+b$) does not control the components separately. Counterexample: $\Omega=\Omega_1\cup\Omega_2$ disjoint, $\Gamma\subset\partial\Omega_1$ satisfying the assumption, $\bu=0$ on $\Omega_1$ and $\bu=\bb\neq 0$ constant on $\Omega_2$: then $\BD\bu=0$ and $\tr(\bu)\cdot\bn=0$ on $\Gamma$, but $\|\bu\|_{W^{1,p}}>0$, so (eq:kornetto0) fails. Summing over components requires the assumption on each $\Gamma\cap\partial\Omega_i$.

failure_location.quote: The same conclusion holds true if $\Omega\subset\R^{d}$ is open and bounded with Lipschitz boundary and has finitely many connected components.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require Assumption assump:dom on $\Gamma\cap\partial\Omega_i$ for each connected component $\Omega_i$ (with $\mathcal{R}$ understood componentwise), or delete the supplementary sentence.
issues.overall_effect: Only the supplementary claim about domains with several connected components is false; the connected case and all applications (polyhedral connected domains) are unaffected.
issues.title: Korn inequality supplementary statement fails for disconnected domains with the given Assumption
issues.why_classification: A peripheral, unused generalisation; a one-line hypothesis correction restores it and nothing else in the paper depends on it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: suppose that $\pi(x)\coloneqq Ax+b$ satisfies $\pi=0$ on $\Gamma$, whereby $\pi=0$ on $H_{1}\cup H_{2}$.

Thanks to Corollary~\ref{cor:polyhedral},

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption assump:dom requires that $\brho\cdot\bn=0$ on $\Gamma$ forces $\brho=0$; the proof instead assumes the much stronger $\pi=0$ on $\Gamma$ and then argues incoherently. The statement itself is false for $d\geq 3$: take the unit cube, $\Gamma_1$ the face $\{x_3=0\}$, $\Gamma_2$ the face $\{x_1=0\}$ (non-collinear normals), and the translation $\brho\equiv e_2$; then $\brho\cdot\bn=0$ on $\Gamma_1\cup\Gamma_2$ although $\brho\neq 0$. Two hyperplanes with non-collinear normals kill neither translations parallel to $H_1\cap H_2$ nor (in general) the assumption; one needs normals spanning $\R^d$. (In $d=2$ the statement happens to hold.)

issues.failure_explanation:
The identity $(\PiSZ v)\cdot n=\PiSZ( v\cdot n)$ requires $ n$ to be constant on the whole boundary; on a polyhedron $ n$ jumps across edges/corners. At a boundary node $z$ shared by faces $F_1,F_2$ with different normals, the componentwise Scott–Zhang nodal value $\int_{F_1}\psi_z v$ satisfies $\int_{F_1}\psi_z v\cdot n_1=0$ but in general $\int_{F_1}\psi_z v\cdot n_2
eq 0$ (e.g. $d=2$, square, corner $z=(0,0)$, $ v=(x_1^2\chi,0)\in H^1_{ n}$ gives $(\PiSZ v)_1(z)=-h^2/6
eq 0$), so $\PiSZ v\cdot n
eq 0$ on $F_2$. Also $\PiSZ$ maps into $\mathcal{L}^1_1$, so the claimed equality with $X_h\cap H^1_{ n}$ cannot hold when $X_h\supsetneq\mathcal{L}^1_1$. Consequently, in the limit passage the pressure–normal-trace term $\langle\pi^k, v_h\cdot nangle_\Gamma$ and the Nitsche terms with $ v_h\cdot n$ do not vanish as asserted and are not controlled.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $\PiSZ$ for the smooth test fields $\bv\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega)^d$ with $\bv\cdot\bn=0$ by the nodal Lagrange interpolant $I_h\bv\in\mathcal{L}^1_1(\tria)^d$: since $\bv$ is continuous, $\bv(z)\cdot\bn_F=0$ at every node $z$ of every boundary face $F$, so $I_h\bv\cdot\bn=0$ on $\Gamma$, and $I_h\bv\to\bv$ in $H^1$ with $\|\nabla I_h\bv\|_{L^2(\Gamma)}\lesssim\|\bv\|_{W^{2,\infty}}$ by standard local estimates (replacing Corollary cor:SZ-stab). Correct Lemma lem:SZ (ii) accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: Step 1 of Proposition prop:limit-eq (distributional limit equation) drops boundary terms that are actually present; as written the limit passage is incomplete.
issues.title: Scott–Zhang interpolant does not preserve zero normal trace at corners/edges
issues.why_classification: A labelled lemma is false and the limit passage relies on it, but a contained replacement construction (Lagrange interpolation of smooth test functions) restores every claim without changing the method or results.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma lem:p-est only gives $\delta_k^2\sum_j\|\pi_j^k\|^{p}\le c$ with $p=8/(d+4)<2$ (the extra factor $\delta_k$ is forced by the term $\delta_k^{-1}\|\bu_j^k-\bu_{j-1}^k\|_B$, which is not bounded in $\ell^p$ against $\delta_k$). This does not bound $\xi^k(t)=\int_0^t\pi^k$: $\|\xi^k(t)\|_{L^2}\le\delta_k\sum_j\|\pi_j^k\|_{L^2}\le\delta_k\, m_k^{1-1/p}(\sum_j\|\pi_j^k\|^p)^{1/p}\lesssim\delta_k^{-1/p}$ by Hölder, which diverges. Hence eq:est-press-4 and the weak convergence eq:conv-xi are not established as written, and the pressure term in the limit passage is unjustified.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Bound $\xi^k_j=\delta_k\sum_{i\le j}\pi^k_i$ directly by summing the discrete equation in time: for $\bv_h\in X_h\cap H^1_0$, $\langle\xi^k_j,\div\bv_h\rangle=-(\bu^k_j-\bu^k_0,\bv_h)_B+\delta_k\sum_{i\le j}z_2(\bu^k_i,\bv_h)$, and use the a priori bounds ($\|\bu^k_j-\bu^k_0\|_B\le c$, $\delta_k\sum_i\|\bu_i^k\|_{L^4}\|\bu_i^k\|_{H^1}\le c$) with the discrete inf-sup condition to obtain $\|\xi^k\|_{L^\infty(I;L^2)}\le c$; then proceed as in the lemma.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence of $\int_0^T\pi^k\phi^k$ used in Step 1 of Proposition prop:limit-eq (needed because the Scott–Zhang test functions are not discretely divergence-free) lacks a valid bound; the remark on pressure regularity is likewise unsupported by the given chain.
issues.title: Bound on the time-integrated pressure does not follow from the pressure estimate
issues.why_classification: The inference is invalid and a replacement estimate (a new, though standard, summed-in-time argument) is required; the conclusion and all dependent results survive unchanged once it is supplied.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: While in space we have full admissibility, in time some integrability is missing due to the convective term.
This can be derived by the energy identity in Proposition~\ref{prop:limit-eq} and the corresponding energy inequality for $\bu^k$.
Because only some integrability in time is lacking, but full admissibility in space is available, no truncation technique is needed.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either restrict the energy-identity statement and Theorem thm:main-unsteady-v to $d=2$ (or to the range of $r$ in $d=3$ for which strong $L^r(I\times\Gamma)$ convergence of traces can be obtained by interpolation, roughly $r<8/3$, using Lemma lem:conv-simple instead), or supply a new argument (e.g. a truncation technique) yielding the required lower bound on $\limsup\int\hat\bsigma^k\cdot\tr_\tau\bu^k$ in $d=3$.
issues.overall_effect: For $d=2$ the identity holds ($\bu\in L^4(I;L^4)$) and Theorem thm:main-unsteady-v stands. For $d=3$, the identification of the implicit boundary relation for $r\in(2,4)$ via the Minty argument is unsupported, so Theorem thm:main-unsteady-v (and the meta theorem's claim of covering $r<2^\sharp=4$ in 3D) is not established. Theorem thm:main-unsteady ($r\le 2$) does not use the energy identity and is unaffected.
issues.title: Energy identity for the limit is unjustified in d=3, undermining the r>2 identification
issues.why_classification: An advertised regime ($d=3$, $r\in(2,4)$) is excluded or requires essentially new proof architecture; the claimed energy identity in 3D has no supported proof.
